title: Who this residence is
rule: Residence for international telework is a third-country national authorised to remain in Spain to carry out a labour or professional activity at a distance for companies established outside Spain, using exclusively computer, telematic and telecommunication means.

title: Union citizens are outside this law
rule: Section 2 of Title V of Ley 14/2013 does not apply to EU citizens or to foreigners who enjoy equivalent free-movement rights under EU agreements.

title: Employed vs professional: the 20% ceiling
rule: If the activity is labour (employed), the holder may work only for companies established outside Spain. If the activity is professional, work for a company in Spain is allowed only if that work is not more than 20% of total professional activity.

title: Qualified professionals
rule: The visa or authorisation may be requested by qualified professionals who prove they are graduates or postgraduates of universities of recognised prestige, vocational training, or business schools of recognised prestige, or who have a minimum of three years’ professional experience.
packetItem: Degree/postgraduate diploma from a university, VET centre or business school of recognised prestige — or evidence of at least three years’ professional experience in functions analogous to the remote role.

title: The foreign company must have one year of real activity
rule: Prove real and continuous activity for at least one year of the company or group with which the worker has a labour or professional relationship.
packetItem: Certificate from the companies register (or equivalent body) showing date of incorporation (not less than one year) and type of activity.

title: The work can actually be done remotely
rule: File evidence that the labour or professional relationship can be performed remotely.
packetItem: Written proof that the role is performed exclusively by computer, telematic and telecommunication means.

title: Employed: three months’ relationship plus remote permission
rule: For a labour relationship, prove that it has existed with the non-Spanish company for at least the three months before filing, and that the company permits remote work.
packetItem: Employer certificate: seniority (minimum three months) and express permission to work remotely from Spain, stating profile, salary, and terms.

title: Professional: three months’ mercantile relationship plus terms
rule: For a professional relationship, prove a mercantile relationship with one or more companies not located in Spain for at least the last three months, and the terms on which the remote professional activity will be exercised.
packetItem: Mercantile contracts / invoices covering at least three months, plus a document setting the remote terms and conditions.

title: General Ley 14/2013 requirements also apply
rule: In addition to art. 74 ter, the general requirements of art. 62 apply: not irregular in Spain; over 18; criminal record; not listed as inadmissible; health insurance; sufficient resources for the holder and family; payment of the fee.

title: Eighteen or older
rule: The applicant must be over 18.

title: Not in an irregular situation in Spain
rule: The applicant must not be in an irregular situation in Spanish territory.

title: Criminal record: two-year certificates plus five-year sworn declaration
rule: No criminal record in Spain or in the countries of residence during the last two years, for offences under Spanish law. In addition, file a sworn declaration of no criminal record covering the last five years. The joint instruction restates this packet: certificates for the last two years of residence, plus the five-year declaration. The official FAQ states the two-year certificates plus five-year declaration are not required where the person already holds a Spanish residence or stay authorisation of more than six months.
packetItem: Criminal-record certificates from each country of residence in the last two years (apostilled or legalised, sworn translation) + sworn declaration covering five years.

title: Not listed as inadmissible
rule: The applicant must not appear as inadmissible (rechazable) in the territory of countries with which Spain has signed an agreement to that effect.

title: Public or authorised private sickness insurance
rule: Art. 62.3.e requires public insurance or private sickness insurance contracted with an insurer authorised to operate in Spain. The official UGE FAQ adds operational limits: travel insurance is not valid; policies limited to reimbursement of medical expenses are not valid; policies with waiting periods or co-payments are not valid. Public cover through registration in Spanish Social Security also satisfies the requirement.
packetItem: Certificate of public cover (SS registration / bilateral coverage certificate) or a private full-cover policy with an insurer authorised in Spain — not travel, not reimbursement-only, no waiting periods, no co-payments.

title: Resources: 200% SMI holder · 75% first family member · 25% each additional
rule: Art. 62.3.f requires sufficient resources for the holder and family. The joint instruction (applying that article) sets the amounts: holder, a monthly amount representing 200% of SMI; family unit of two (holder + first family member), at least 75% of SMI for that first member; 25% of SMI for each additional member. Proof may be any means admitted in law, including the employment contract, firm job offer, or mercantile contract. Ownership, lawfulness and availability of funds used as proof must be accredited. This is a formula. Do not treat this year’s euro arithmetic as the statute — see conflict smi-monthly-conversion.
legalFormula: holder = 200% × SMI (monthly); first family member = 75% × SMI; each additional family member = 25% × SMI
packetItem: Contract, firm offer or mercantile contract showing the remote income, plus any bank evidence of ownership, lawfulness and availability of the funds relied on.

title: Social Security: coverage certificate or Spanish registration commitment
rule: Plataforma ONE and the joint-instruction document list require either a Social Security coverage certificate (where a bilateral agreement applies) or registration / a request to register the foreign company in the Spanish Social Security system, with a commitment to complete registration once the authorisation is granted and before work starts. Art. 76.5 allows the passport to suffice for SS registration during the first six months if the foreigner does not yet hold an NIE.
packetItem: Bilateral SS coverage certificate, or evidence of the request to register the foreign employer in Spanish Social Security plus a responsible declaration to complete alta before activity starts.

title: From abroad: consular visa, not UGE-CE
rule: Foreigners who are not residents in Spain and intend to reside in Spain to telework for a company not located in Spain must apply for the international-telework visa. The official FAQ states it is not possible to apply from abroad directly for the residence authorisation. Apply at the Spanish consular office competent for the country of residence.

title: Visa validity: maximum one year
rule: The international-telework visa has a maximum validity of one year, unless the work period is shorter, in which case the visa has the same validity. The visa is in itself a sufficient title to reside and work remotely in Spain during its validity.

title: Sixty days before the visa expires: apply for the three-year residence
rule: Within sixty calendar days before the visa expires, holders who wish to continue residing in Spain may apply for the international-teleworker residence authorisation, provided the conditions that generated the right remain.

title: Already lawfully in Spain: UGE-CE residence via Plataforma ONE / sede
rule: Foreigners who are in Spain in a regular situation, or who entered on the telework visa, may apply for a residence authorisation to telework for a company located abroad, valid throughout Spain. File electronically with the UGE-CE. Plataforma ONE describes the channel: MI-T (and MI-F for family), pay tasa 038 and obtain an NRC, then submit on the UGE-CE sede with a digital certificate or Cl@ve.

title: Residence validity: maximum three years
rule: The residence authorisation has a maximum validity of three years unless requested for a shorter work period. Plataforma ONE restates: three years, or less if the contract is shorter.

title: Renewal: two-year periods, conditions maintained
rule: Holders may request renewal for two-year periods provided the conditions that generated the right are maintained. Art. 76.3: renewals are electronic; filing extends validity until the decision, including if filed within ninety days after expiry (without prejudice to a possible sanction file).

title: UGE-CE decides in twenty days; silence is positive
rule: Maximum decision period is twenty days from electronic filing with the competent body. If not decided in that period, the authorisation is granted by administrative silence. The pending stay or residence is extended until the decision. Decisions are reasoned and may be appealed in alzada.

title: Forms: MI-T (holder) and MI-F (each family member)
rule: Plataforma ONE: download, complete and sign the holder residence form (MI-T). For family, complete MI-F for each member and file jointly.
packetItem: Signed MI-T (holder). Signed MI-F for each family member if they file with you.

title: Forms: national visa application, signed by the teleworker
rule: The joint instruction and consular pages require the visa application form signed by the teleworker. Use the current national visa form published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, plus any local copies the competent consulate lists on its page.
packetItem: National visa application form, completed and signed (copies as the competent consulate currently requires).

title: Fee: modelo 790, code 038, paid before filing, keep the NRC
rule: Plataforma ONE and the official FAQ: pay tasa 038 before starting the electronic file (card, direct debit or Bizum, or bank). Keep the NRC (Número de Referencia Completo) for the submission. The euro amount lives on the official fee page and in the current FAQ — it is a fee tariff, not a statutory income threshold, and it changes. Read the live tasa 038 page on the day you pay.
packetItem: Proof of payment of tasa 038 and the NRC.

title: Consular visa fee: the post’s current tariff
rule: Art. 62.3.g requires payment of the visa or authorisation fee. The amount is the consular tariff in force at that post, not a figure frozen in this codex. Do not copy euro or dollar amounts from old consular PDFs.
packetItem: Receipt of the national-visa fee as charged by the competent consulate on the day of filing.

title: Complete passport copy
rule: The joint instruction requires a copy of the complete valid passport or travel document (all pages).
packetItem: Full-colour copy of every passport page, plus the original at the consular appointment.

title: Apostille or legalisation, then sworn translation
rule: Foreign public documents must be apostilled under the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961, or legalised through the Spanish consular/MAE channel, unless an international agreement exempts them. Documents must be translated into Spanish by a sworn translator. Follow the ministry legalisation-and-translation sheet — not blog checklists.
packetItem: Each foreign public document: apostille or legalisation + sworn Spanish translation, filed behind the source document.

title: TIE if the authorisation lasts more than six months
rule: Once the authorisation is granted, if it has a validity of more than six months, the foreigner must apply for the TIE (tarjeta de identidad de extranjero). File personally at the competent police unit. Use the current official TIE appointment channel.

title: What this authorisation does not permit
rule: An employed holder may not work for companies established in Spain. A professional holder may not let Spanish-sited work exceed 20% of total professional activity. Authorisations and visas under this section will be revoked, refused or not renewed if the foreigner may represent a threat to public order, public security, public health or national security, on the basis of a police, CNI or National Security Department report.
